overview_pre: **Counselling and recognition only**: what procedures are, expectations, safety and referral. Not a procedure how-to.
kf: **Chemical peels**: controlled chemical injury to epidermis ± dermis (superficial, medium, deep).
**Microneedling**: fine needles cause micro-injuries that trigger new collagen.
**Lasers**: **selective photothermolysis**, a wavelength targets water, haemoglobin or melanin.
Darker skin types have a higher risk of **post-inflammatory pigmentation** and scarring: choose operators carefully.
Isotretinoin: document it and **let the operating clinician decide** on timing; HSV history may need antiviral cover.
myths: **"Home microneedling is the same as clinic treatment"**: home devices are shorter and carry infection risk.
patho_lead: Most resurfacing procedures **injure the skin in a controlled way** so it repairs with new collagen.

mech.t: Peels, needles and ablative lasers damage set depths of skin.
Inflammation, then fibroblasts lay down new collagen over months.
Lasers heat one chromophore (melanin, haemoglobin, water) and spare the rest.
Deeper injury gives more effect, more downtime and more risk.

comp: PIH, scarring, infection, HSV reactivation, burns, eye injury (lasers).
prog: Results build over 3–6 months; repeat sessions are common.
